source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-17: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 17 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Define the architecture and evaluation contract before choosing an implementation. Assume a multi-node NVIDIA Dynamo-like service with separate frontend, prefill, and decode roles, but verify the exact product/version and supported APIs; do not invent platform facts. This is evaluation variant 17 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.. Record model and tokenizer revisions, GPU/NIC and PCIe/NUMA topology, RDMA provider, failure domains, memory limits, deployment configuration, prompt/output distributions, concurrency, batching, cache state, and tenant policy. Label every unavailable item evidence_required.

Trace one request end to end: frontend admission and routing select compatible workers; prefill creates KV identified by model revision, tokenizer, layer/head/position, dtype, shape, namespace, and epoch; decode consumes it only after schema, checksum, lease/freshness, authorization, and tenant-isolation checks. Document KV ownership, serialization and transport, placement/replication, queueing, scheduling, quotas/backpressure, expiry/eviction, and observability. Separate compute, queue, KV-transfer, serialization, and control-plane time; report throughput (requests/s and tokens/s), time-to-first-token and inter-token latency (ms), p50/p95/p99, GPU/NIC utilization, bytes/request, queue depth, error/retry/fallback rates, and quality/output-integrity checks.

Pre-register the falsifiable hypothesis: under the stated workload and fixed model, quality, sampling, hardware budget, and concurrency, disaggregation improves the selected latency or throughput metric by a stated margin without violating error, isolation, or output-integrity limits. Compare against a matched colocated baseline and, where relevant, a conventional non-disaggregated baseline; use warm/cold and cache-hit/miss strata, synchronized clocks, repeated randomized trials, confidence intervals, and cost/power accounting. Attribute gains only after sensitivity analysis for batching, routing, cache state, network contention, NUMA placement, and autoscaling.

Exercise bounded failures: inject worker loss, RDMA timeout, stale/corrupt/incompatible KV, queue overload, NIC/link degradation, and control-plane unavailability. Expect fencing, bounded retries with deadlines, cancellation, tenant-safe cache rejection, admission backpressure, and fallback to a known-good path. Roll back or disable the feature if p99 or error budget breaches the pre-registered gate, output checks fail, isolation is uncertain, or telemetry cannot distinguish layers; preserve logs and configuration hashes. No performance claim is justified until the inventory, matched measurements, fault results, and raw traces are available.

source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-28: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 28 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Use a dry-run, permission-checked workflow; do not execute deployment or traffic-changing commands until evidence and rollback are ready. Assume a multi-node NVIDIA Dynamo-like service with separate frontend, prefill, and decode roles, but verify the exact product/version and supported APIs; do not invent platform facts. This is evaluation variant 28 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.. Record model and tokenizer revisions, GPU/NIC and PCIe/NUMA topology, RDMA provider, failure domains, memory limits, deployment configuration, prompt/output distributions, concurrency, batching, cache state, and tenant policy. Label every unavailable item evidence_required.

Trace one request end to end: frontend admission and routing select compatible workers; prefill creates KV identified by model revision, tokenizer, layer/head/position, dtype, shape, namespace, and epoch; decode consumes it only after schema, checksum, lease/freshness, authorization, and tenant-isolation checks. Document KV ownership, serialization and transport, placement/replication, queueing, scheduling, quotas/backpressure, expiry/eviction, and observability. Separate compute, queue, KV-transfer, serialization, and control-plane time; report throughput (requests/s and tokens/s), time-to-first-token and inter-token latency (ms), p50/p95/p99, GPU/NIC utilization, bytes/request, queue depth, error/retry/fallback rates, and quality/output-integrity checks.

Pre-register the falsifiable hypothesis: under the stated workload and fixed model, quality, sampling, hardware budget, and concurrency, disaggregation improves the selected latency or throughput metric by a stated margin without violating error, isolation, or output-integrity limits. Compare against a matched colocated baseline and, where relevant, a conventional non-disaggregated baseline; use warm/cold and cache-hit/miss strata, synchronized clocks, repeated randomized trials, confidence intervals, and cost/power accounting. Attribute gains only after sensitivity analysis for batching, routing, cache state, network contention, NUMA placement, and autoscaling.

Exercise bounded failures: inject worker loss, RDMA timeout, stale/corrupt/incompatible KV, queue overload, NIC/link degradation, and control-plane unavailability. Expect fencing, bounded retries with deadlines, cancellation, tenant-safe cache rejection, admission backpressure, and fallback to a known-good path. Roll back or disable the feature if p99 or error budget breaches the pre-registered gate, output checks fail, isolation is uncertain, or telemetry cannot distinguish layers; preserve logs and configuration hashes. No performance claim is justified until the inventory, matched measurements, fault results, and raw traces are available.
